note: Margin and spacing tokens have no effect on SEO or screen reader behavior. What actually matters for both is the semantic HTML element each typography style renders as. This file maps each existing style to its correct element.

display large.use: The single main page title. One per page, for SEO and screen reader page structure.

display medium.use: Alternate h1 size for a shorter hero context.

display small.use: Alternate h1 size for a compact hero context.

label large.element: span with aria-label on its control
label large.use: Button and form control text, not a heading.

label medium.element: span with aria-label on its control
label medium.use: Smaller button and form control text.

label small.element: span with aria-label on its control
label small.use: Smallest button and form control text.

rules: Never skip a heading level (h1 to h3 with no h2) purely to get a smaller visual size. Pick the style whose visual size matches the correct semantic level instead.
Every non-text control (icon-only button, image used as a link) needs an aria-label or alt text, the typography role alone does not provide this.
font-family and font-weight must never be the only way meaning is conveyed (e.g. bold alone signaling 'required'). Screen readers do not reliably announce style, only structure and explicit text.
Set lang on the html element so screen readers pick the correct pronunciation and font fallback (Poppins and DM Sans both already have fallback stacks defined).
